text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- During his visit to Beijing, Danish foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen held two meetings Monday with Chinese government chief Li Peng, his foreign minister and the deputy speaker of China's parliament. At the meeting Denmark brought up the issues of human rights in China and parliamentary cooperation on legal questions between the two countries.

--- The Danish section of the international biker group Hell's Angels has agreed to move to new headquarters offered by the Copenhagen authorities further away from residential areas amid fears of an escalation of its ongoing war with rival Bandidos gang in Scandinavia.
--- Danish biotechnology and pharmaceuticals group Novo Nordisk A/S is to invest 1.3 billion crowns in a new China headquarters and research centre near Beijing due for completion in spring 1997.
--- A group of four Danish fishing firms in northern Denmark has won a 100 million crown contract to provide equipment for a new fisheries centre in Malaysia.

--- Danish Maersk Air is to buy three new Boeing 737-500SP passenger aircraft to the tune of some four billion crowns within the next five years for use in charter holiday operations which account for a quarter of the airline's activities.

--- Three-quarters of Danish export companies now no longer have to report trade data to Intrastat, the European Union's statistical office, a major administrative relief for the country's importers and exporters, Denmark's Chamber of Commerce and the Danish Confederation of Industry say in unison.
